summary: AstraBase is an interactive web based STEM simulator built with React, Tailwind CSS, and Lucide React. Players play the role as an outpost commander managing a lunar or Martian base, balancing power, life support, radiation shielding, and payload mass through a live 2D page. Real space exploration requires managing strict competing constraints but AstraBase forces players to experience real world engineering trade offs like balancing heavy nuclear reactors against vulnerable solar panels during 14 day lunar nights, or even managing payload mass against long term closed loop recycling. This project bridges the gap between textbook science and practical systems engineering because it lets students test variables, analyze and observe different mission failures, and export reports. It promotes critical thinking and makes complex aerospace physics easy to use and engaging for the classroom.
details:
AstraBase isn’t just a game. It’s an interactive, web-based STEM tool built to teach high schoolers the brutal reality of engineering trade-offs in permanent off-world habitats on the Moon or Mars. You play as an Outpost Commander. The system is turn-based. Your job? Balance five core pillars: Power Grid (Solar vs. Kilopower Nuclear), Life Support (Open vs. Closed-Loop ECLSS), Radiation Shielding (Regolith and Water Walls), Payload Mass budgeting, and Crew Health/Morale.

An interactive 2D base schematic updates visually based on your choices. NASA engineering tooltips verify the data. Dynamic non-repeating events keep things unpredictable. An automated student debrief report grades performance and formats assignment submissions. This addresses the fundamental challenge of space exploration: managing strict, competing constraints under harsh extraterrestrial environments. Players balance limited payload mass against long-term survival requirements—like surviving the 14-day lunar night or Martian dust storms without losing power or crew health. It bridges the gap between abstract textbook physics and practical systems engineering. Modern STEM education needs this. It fosters systems thinking. It builds critical problem-solving skills. It gives teachers a classroom-ready tool to gamify aerospace science.

The tech stack is React, Tailwind CSS, and Lucide React for icons. Developed locally inside the Cursor AI-assisted code editor. Run on a Vite React environment. Academic rigor was non-negotiable. The simulation integrates official data from verified space programs. NASA Kilopower Reactor Project (KRUSTY) provides fission power parameters. The ISS Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS) dictates metabolic rates and Sabatier recycling efficiencies. The NASA Space Radiation Analysis Group (SRAG) supplies cosmic ray baselines and regolith shielding attenuation models.

AstraBase turns complex aerospace engineering data into an engaging, gamified sandbox. Cinematic sci-fi prologue. Interactive tutorials. Live 2D base visualizer. Custom failure-analysis debrief system. Throughout development, the team prioritized classroom usability. Every variable adheres to realistic physics. Intuitive. Responsive. Fully accessible to students and educators.
